name: Dandelion
botanicalFact: Dandelion seeds can drift for miles on the wind, and bees love the flowers.

nameStory.line: Dandelion comes from “lion's tooth.”
nameStory.funFact: Look at a leaf. Its sharp, pointy edges look like a row of lion teeth.

name: Daisy
botanicalFact: Its name comes from 'day's eye': petals close at night.

nameStory.line: Daisy comes from “day's eye.”
nameStory.funFact: Its petals close at night and open with the morning sun, like an eye waking up.

name: Clover
botanicalFact: Clover's root bacteria turn nitrogen from the air into plant food for the soil.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Trifolium, means “three leaves.”
nameStory.funFact: Look for leaves made of three round parts. A rare clover has four!

name: Marigold
botanicalFact: Roots release compounds that deter harmful nematodes.

nameStory.line: Marigold comes from “Mary's gold.”
nameStory.funFact: Its petals glow gold and orange. They look like small gold coins.

name: Sunflower
botanicalFact: Young blooms track the sun: heliotropism.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Helianthus, means “sun flower.”
nameStory.funFact: Its big round head with gold petals looks like a bright sun.

name: Tulip
botanicalFact: Tulip bulbs fueled a speculative price bubble in the Netherlands in the 1630s.

nameStory.line: Tulip comes from an old word for “turban.”
nameStory.funFact: A turban is a long cloth that is wrapped around the head. People thought an open tulip looked like one.

name: Rose
botanicalFact: Its fruits, called rose hips, are rich in vitamin C.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Rosa gallica, means “rose of Gaul.”
nameStory.funFact: Gaul is an old name for the land of France. So people also call it the French rose.

name: Poppy
botanicalFact: Poppy seeds can sleep in the soil for many years. They wake and grow when the soil is dug up.

name: Fern
botanicalFact: Ferns reproduce with spores rather than seeds or flowers.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Nephrolepis, means “kidney scale.”
nameStory.funFact: Look under a leaf for tiny dots shaped like kidney beans. They hold specks that grow new ferns.

name: Strawberry
botanicalFact: The tiny 'seeds' on its surface are actually separate fruits; the red flesh is an enlarged flower base.

nameStory.line: Strawberry is “straw” plus “berry.”
nameStory.funFact: No one knows for sure why. It may be for its thin runners, which look like bits of straw.

name: Orchid
botanicalFact: One of the two largest flowering plant families.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Phalaenopsis, means “like a moth.”
nameStory.funFact: Its wide, flat flowers look like moths in flight. That is why it is called the moth orchid.

name: Lavender
botanicalFact: People have used lavender for scent and bathing for thousands of years.

name: Lotus
botanicalFact: Leaves repel water: the 'lotus effect'.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, nucifera, means “nut bearing.”
nameStory.funFact: Its seed pod looks like a round cup full of holes. Each hole holds a seed like a little nut.

name: Jasmine
botanicalFact: Blooms release most scent at night.

name: Snapdragon
botanicalFact: Squeeze a bloom's sides and the 'dragon' opens its mouth.

nameStory.line: Snapdragon means a “snapping dragon.”
nameStory.funFact: Gently squeeze the sides of a flower. Its “mouth” opens and shuts like a dragon's.

name: Saguaro Cactus
botanicalFact: A saguaro often waits 50 to 70 years before it grows its first arm.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, gigantea, means “giant.”
nameStory.funFact: It can grow taller than a house, with arms that reach up to the sky.

name: Aloe Vera
botanicalFact: Its thick leaves store a water-rich gel inside.

nameStory.line: Vera means “true.”
nameStory.funFact: Many kinds of aloe look alike. This one was called the true aloe. Its leaves hold a cool, clear gel.

name: Bamboo
botanicalFact: Giant moso bamboo can grow about a meter in one day.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, edulis, means “good to eat.”
nameStory.funFact: People cook its young shoots. You may have had bamboo shoots in a meal!

name: Hibiscus
botanicalFact: Each bloom typically lasts about a day.

nameStory.line: Hibiscus comes from the Greek word “hibiskos.”
nameStory.funFact: The Greeks gave that name to the marsh mallow plant. Its root was once used to make marshmallows!

name: Cherry Blossom
botanicalFact: Japan's hanami custom of viewing the blossoms is centuries old.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, serrulata, means “little saw teeth.”
nameStory.funFact: Look at the edge of a leaf. It has tiny points, like the teeth on a saw.

name: Venus Flytrap
botanicalFact: Traps shut in about 0.1s when two hairs are touched.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, muscipula, means “mousetrap.”
nameStory.funFact: Its leaves snap shut like a tiny trap. They catch bugs, not mice!

name: Baobab
botanicalFact: Big baobab trunks can store over 100,000 liters of water.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Adansonia, is for Michel Adanson.
nameStory.funFact: He was from France. In 1749 he went to Senegal and saw the big baobab trees there.

name: Corpse Flower
botanicalFact: Smells like rotting flesh to attract pollinators.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, titanum, means “giant.”
nameStory.funFact: Its flower spike can grow taller than a grown-up. It has a strong, stinky smell that flies love!

name: Welwitschia
botanicalFact: Grows just two leaves in its life, for 1,000+ years.

nameStory.line: It is named for Friedrich Welwitsch.
nameStory.funFact: He found it in Angola in 1859. He was so amazed that he knelt down to look at it.

name: Dragon Blood Tree
botanicalFact: Its bark bleeds a deep red resin.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Dracaena, means “she-dragon.”
nameStory.funFact: Its sap is deep red. Long ago, people called it “dragon's blood.”

name: Pitcher Plant
botanicalFact: Its pitcher-shaped leaves hold digestive fluid that drowns insects.

nameStory.line: A pitcher is a jug, and its leaves look like one.
nameStory.funFact: Each leaf makes a deep cup with a lid. Small bugs slip in and get trapped.

name: Sensitive Plant
botanicalFact: Its leaflets fold shut within seconds of being touched.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, pudica, means “shy.”
nameStory.funFact: Touch a leaf and it folds up fast, as if it is shy. Soon it opens up again.

name: Bird of Paradise
botanicalFact: Native to South Africa, its bloom resembles a colorful bird's head.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, reginae, means “of the queen.”
nameStory.funFact: It was named for Queen Charlotte of Britain. Its flower looks like a bright bird with a crest.

name: Joshua Tree
botanicalFact: It depends on yucca moths for pollination.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, brevifolia, means “short leaves.”
nameStory.funFact: Its leaves are short and spiky. They grow in bunches at the tips of the branches.

name: Lithops
botanicalFact: These 'living stones' from southern Africa are camouflaged to look like pebbles.

nameStory.line: Lithops means “stone face.”
nameStory.funFact: These small plants look like rocks. Hungry animals walk past and do not see them.

name: Rafflesia
botanicalFact: Produces the world's largest single flower, about a meter across.

nameStory.line: It is named for Sir Stamford Raffles.
nameStory.funFact: He and his friend Joseph Arnold saw it in Sumatra in 1818. Its flower can be as wide as a hula hoop!

name: Monkey Puzzle Tree
botanicalFact: Native to Chile and Argentina, it is the national tree of Chile.

nameStory.line: A man joked it would puzzle a monkey to climb it.
nameStory.funFact: Its branches are covered in sharp, stiff leaves. A monkey would find it hard to climb.

name: Sago Palm
botanicalFact: Despite the name it is not a palm but a cycad, an ancient seed-plant lineage. Every part is poisonous, so never eat it.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, revoluta, means “curled back.”
nameStory.funFact: Look at the edge of a leaflet. It curls back under, like a rolled-up sleeve.

name: Ghost Pipe
botanicalFact: It has no chlorophyll and draws nutrients through fungi linked to tree roots.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Monotropa, means “one turn.”
nameStory.funFact: Each stem bends over at the top and holds one flower. It is pale white, like candle wax.

name: Passionflower
botanicalFact: Its name comes from Spanish missionaries who saw symbols of the Passion in the bloom.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, caerulea, means “sky blue.”
nameStory.funFact: Look for the ring of thin threads in the flower. They are blue, white and purple.

name: King Protea
botanicalFact: It is the national flower of South Africa.

nameStory.line: Protea is named for Proteus, who could change shape.
nameStory.funFact: Proteus was a sea god in old Greek tales. Protea flowers come in many shapes, just like him.

name: Bleeding Heart
botanicalFact: Native to Siberia, northern China, Korea and Japan.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, spectabilis, means “worth seeing.”
nameStory.funFact: Each pink flower looks like a little heart with a white drop below it. Look for a row on one stem.

name: Giant Water Lily
botanicalFact: Its floating leaves can exceed 2 m across.

nameStory.line: It is named for Queen Victoria of Britain.
nameStory.funFact: Its round leaves float on the water. They can be wider than a bed.

name: Sundew
botanicalFact: Sticky tentacles on its leaves trap and digest small insects.

nameStory.line: Sundew comes from “dew of the sun.”
nameStory.funFact: Its leaves shine with sticky drops that look like dew in the sun. Small bugs stick to them.

name: Lady's Slipper Orchid
botanicalFact: Its slipper-shaped pouch acts as a trap that guides insects past the pollen.

nameStory.line: Its plant name means “slipper of Aphrodite.”
nameStory.funFact: Aphrodite was a goddess in old Greek tales. The flower has a puffy pouch shaped like a slipper.

name: Wollemi Pine
botanicalFact: Scientists knew it from fossils until living trees were found in Australia in 1994.

nameStory.line: It is named for a park called Wollemi.
nameStory.funFact: The park is in Australia. A man named David Noble found it there in 1994. Its second name is for him.

name: Jade Vine
botanicalFact: Its turquoise, claw-shaped flowers are pollinated by bats.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, macrobotrys, means “long grape bunch.”
nameStory.funFact: Its flowers hang in long bunches like grapes. They are the blue-green of jade.

name: Coco de Mer
botanicalFact: It produces the heaviest seed of any plant.

nameStory.line: Coco de mer means “coconut of the sea.”
nameStory.funFact: Long ago, big nuts washed up on beaches. People thought the tree grew under the sea.

name: Black Bat Flower
botanicalFact: Long whisker-like bracts dangle from its near-black blooms.

nameStory.line: Its dark flower looks like a bat with open wings.
nameStory.funFact: Long thin threads hang from it like whiskers. Count the wings and the whiskers.

name: Franklin Tree
botanicalFact: It has not been seen in the wild since the early 1800s; all living trees descend from cultivated ones.

nameStory.line: It is named for Benjamin Franklin.
nameStory.funFact: A dad and son found it by a river in 1765. The son named it for a friend, Ben Franklin.

name: Chocolate Cosmos
botanicalFact: Extinct in the wild, its blooms smell of chocolate.

nameStory.line: Cosmos comes from a Greek word for “orderly.”
nameStory.funFact: Its petals sit in a neat ring. This one is dark red-brown and smells like chocolate.

name: Ghost Orchid
botanicalFact: It has no leaves and photosynthesizes through its roots.

nameStory.line: It is called “ghost” because its flower seems to float.
nameStory.funFact: It has no leaves. Its roots blend in with the tree bark, so the white flower seems to float.

name: Silversword
botanicalFact: Native to Hawaii, high on its volcanic slopes.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, Argyroxiphium, means “silver sword.”
nameStory.funFact: Fine silver hairs cover its long, thin leaves. They reflect the strong sun and help it hold water.

name: Rainbow Eucalyptus
botanicalFact: Bark peels in strips at different times, revealing multicolored layers.

nameStory.line: Its plant name, deglupta, means “peeled.”
nameStory.funFact: Its bark peels off in strips. Under it are bright stripes of green, blue, orange and red.

name: Puya raimondii
botanicalFact: The largest bromeliad flowers once after many decades, then sets seed.

nameStory.line: It is named for Antonio Raimondi.
nameStory.funFact: He studied plants in Peru. This puya grows a flower spike as tall as a house.
